transcript.text: theres a funny smell from my oven when its on

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Do not use the oven again until it has been checked by a qualified appliance engineer/electrician. A smell only when heating can be something simple such as old grease, a spill or cleaner residue, but it can also be an overheating electrical connection, wiring or heating element, which is not safe to keep testing. With the oven fully cool and isolated at the cooker switch, you can safely:
1. Look inside the cavity for burnt food, grease, foil, packaging or cleaner residue, particularly on the base and around the element. This would point more towards contamination burning off.
2. Look for any smoke marks, melted plastic, or scorching visible inside the oven. Do not remove panels or inspect fixed electrical connections. If the smell is acrid, electrical/plastic-like, or there is smoke, scorching, tripping of the electrics or intermittent power, treat it as an electrical fault and arrange an engineer without using it again.

nothing in the oven that I can see. the smell is more like hot plastic or electrical, coming from the back or underneath, not inside. the cooker switch looks a bit brown at one corner and felt warm, and the lights flickered once

⚠ Stop using this appliance
This is most likely an overheating connection at the cooker switch or its fixed wiring, rather than residue in the oven. Browning at the switch, warmth and a lights flicker point to a high-resistance electrical connection, which can overheat further when the oven draws power. Do not use the cooker again until it has been checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer. The electrician should inspect the cooker isolator switch, the cable and fixed wiring behind it, and the cooker’s incoming terminal block at the rear. They should also check the oven element and its connections, as an element fault can sometimes contribute to overheating under load. Do not remove the cooker switch faceplate or any oven panels yourself, even with the power off: these are fixed mains connections. If there is any smoke, crackling, worsening smell, or the switch becomes hot, isolate the cooker at the consumer unit if it is safe to do so and arrange urgent electrical attention.

candidates: Food spill, grease or cleaning-product residue burning off (medium)
Residue on a heating element or a failing element (low)

reading.symptom: funny smell when the oven is on

plan: Safety: a burning hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "funny smell when the oven is on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

candidates: Overheating/loose connection at the cooker isolator switch or fixed supply wiring (high)
Burnt mains terminal connection at the rear of the cooker (medium)
Oven heating element or its connector overheating under load (low)
